en: The Sūtra on the Seven Treasures of the Wheel-Turning King,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīlagupta,
Great Master of the Dharma Transmission and Acting Director of the Court of State Ceremonial, under the Imperial Edict during the Western Heaven Dynasty.
Thus have I heard:
At one time, the Buddha was staying in the kingdom of Śrāvastī together with a great assembly of bhikṣus.
At that time, the Buddha addressed the bhikṣus, saying:

"You should know that there appears in the world a great Kṣatriya king who has received the consecration and attained the rank of a Wheel-Turning Monarch (cakravartin), possessing sovereign majesty and power, and revered by all people; when such a king appears, seven treasures manifest."
What are the seven?

They are the wheel-treasure, the elephant-treasure, the horse-treasure, the minister-treasure of the treasury, the minister-treasure of the military, the mani-jewel treasure, and the woman-treasure; these seven treasures appear according to the king's emergence.
"What is called the Wheel-Treasure?

It is a golden wheel with a thousand spokes, most excellent and sublime, perfect in all its characteristics, and possessed of great majesty. This precious golden wheel descends from the sky and comes to rest at the gate of the royal palace. At that time, the Kṣatriya Great Anointed Wheel-Turning King, seeing this Wheel-Treasure appear, is filled with great joy and immediately commands his attendant ministers:
'You must now quickly prepare the fourfold army; we shall go forth on an excursion.'"
At that time, having received the king’s command, the attendant minister immediately prepared the fourfold army. Once it was fully arrayed, he went to the king’s presence and addressed him, saying:
“The fourfold army is ready; this is precisely the right time for Your Majesty to go forth on a pleasure tour.”
At that time, the Kṣatriya Great Anointed Wheel-Turning King rose from his seat, adjusted his robes, and went out through the palace gate;
the thousand-spoked wheel led before the king and revolved in succession along his right hand.
At that time, that king traveled across the four seas and returned to the royal palace in a very short period of time, owing to the superior power of the wheel-treasure.
O Bhikṣus!
This is called the first appearance of the wheel-treasure when a Kṣatriya Great Anointed Wheel-Turning King appears. "Furthermore, monks!

When that Kṣatriya Great Anointed Wheel-Turning King appears, there further appears the elephant-treasure. Its appearance is exquisite and pure white without blemish, like a great dragon; it stands with its seven parts fully and perfectly developed, coming from the north through the air and stopping at the gate of the royal palace."
At that time, when the ministers had witnessed this event, they immediately went to where the king was and reported the matter to him in full detail.
Upon seeing that the elephant-treasure had emerged, the great consecrated wheel-turning monarch was filled with great joy and reflected within himself:
"This is most excellent and supremely distinguished; whatever I may require, I shall certainly take it."
At that time, the king said to his ministers:
"The elephant-treasure has appeared; you should diligently guard it and prepare it for my use.

Having received the king's command, the attendants guarded it with diligent effort over a long period, training it skillfully so that there was not the slightest loss, and they prepared it for the king’s use.
The Buddha told the bhikṣus:

"In the past, there appeared in the world a great Kṣatriya Wheel-Turning King who had received the consecration. At that time, the elephant-treasure also appeared. In the early morning, the king mounted that elephant-treasure and traveled across the four oceans, returning to his palace immediately."
"You should know, monks, that the elephant-treasure possesses such supreme and wondrous efficacy.
This, monks, is called the appearance of the second treasure, the elephant, at the time when a Great Anointed Wheel-Turning King arises."
"Furthermore, monks!

When a Great Anointed Wheel-Turning King appears, there also appears the Horse-Jewel, numbering four in all. Each is complete in its parts and possesses its own exquisite color and marks—namely blue, yellow, red, and white—with necks as beautiful as those of the *mora* bird; they are swift in their gait and well-trained."

When this treasure of the four horses appeared at the palace gate, the ministers and officials, seeing that the horse-treasure was so rare, wonderful, and exquisite, immediately drove it toward the king.
Upon seeing these four horse-treasures, the great consecrated wheel-turning monarch was filled with great joy and reflected within himself:
"The appearance of the horse-treasure is most excellent; whatever I have need of shall surely be accomplished according to my wish."
That great consecrated wheel-turning monarch further proclaimed:
"O you ministers!
For a long time, you must diligently protect and skillfully train it; whenever I have need of it, I shall certainly take it."
At that time, having received the king’s command, the ministers guarded it for a long period, keeping it prepared for the king’s use.

O Bhikṣus! In the past, there was a great consecrated Wheel-Turning King who appeared in the world; at that time, a horse-treasure also appeared. In the early morning, the king mounted this horse-treasure and traveled across the four oceans before returning to his palace.
"You should know, monks, that the horse-treasure possesses such extraordinary power. This, monks,
is called the appearance of the third horse-treasure when a Great Consecrated Wheel-Turning King emerges."
"Furthermore, monks! When a Wheel-Turning King appears, there also appears the Jewel of the Treasurer.
At that time, there is a great treasury, secure and endowed with vast wealth and great riches, which is under the jurisdiction of that minister."
Then the treasurer went to the king and addressed him thus:
"There is a great treasure store, fully endowed with all manner of exquisite and rare jewels, such as gold and every other kind of precious object;
whatever Your Majesty may require, I shall provide it all for you according to your wishes, without the slightest deficiency."

At that time, when the Wheel-Turning King saw that this Jewel of the Steward had emerged, his heart was filled with great joy; furthermore, hearing those words, he obtained all manner of treasures such as gold, fulfilling every great wish.
Then the king spoke to that Jewel of the Steward, saying:

"You now possess such physical marks, supernormal powers, and majestic might that you are able to preside over the vast treasures hidden within the earth, with all manner of jewels, such as gold, fully at your disposal."

Observing such matters, they are truly rare, most excellent, and virtuous; you are a good steward. Whatever I desire, you should provide it; as for other things I do not desire, you may likewise manage them well.

"O Bhikṣus! You should know that as for this terrestrial treasure-store, which is invisible to humans but visible to non-humans, when a Wheel-turning King appears, there emerges a Minister of the Treasury who spontaneously manifests to protect all things for the King and provide every requisite. This is called the appearance of the fourth Treasure, the Minister of the Treasury, at the time of a Wheel-turning King's emergence."
"Furthermore, monks! When a Wheel-Turning King appears, there also appears the Jewel of the Military Commander.

At that time, this minister possesses great wisdom and strategy, as well as courage, valor, and majestic virtue; he is fully endowed with great strength and auspicious physical marks. He skillfully leads the military forces to protect the king’s realm, ensuring it is not invaded or disturbed."
Then the Minister of the Military went to the King’s presence and spoke these words:

"Great King, you should know that I am skilled as the commander of the army and shall protect the royal realm; whether at the proper time or otherwise, whatever needs to be done shall be carried out according to Your Majesty's will, without the slightest deficiency."
At that time, when the king saw that this Jewel of the Commander-in-Chief had appeared, his heart was filled with great joy, and he immediately said to him:
"You now possess great wisdom and strategy, valor, majesty, great power, and an excellent physical form."
Whether at the proper time or otherwise, he is capable of all actions; skillfully leading his military forces, he guards the borders of the kingdom most excellently.
You should assist me closely for a long time; whatever needs to be done, you must employ skillful means. You are now the great protector of the king.
"O Bhikṣus! This is called the appearance of the fifth treasure, the General-Treasure, at the time when a Wheel-Turning King appears.
Furthermore, O Bhikṣus!"
When a Wheel-Turning King appears, there also emerges a great maṇi-jewel.

That maṇi-jewel possesses the most excellent color and form, exquisite and preeminent; it is endowed with a great light that is perfectly complete, its radiance vast and illuminating all things, and it possesses great power.
If such a jewel were within the royal palace, even in the darkness of night where lamps provide no illumination, the jewel would emit its own radiance, shining naturally like the light of the sun.
"O Bhikṣus!
In the past, there appeared a Great Wheel-Turning King in the world, at which time a great maṇi-jewel also appeared, emitting a great radiance.
At that time, the king, wishing to test its power, immediately commanded his ministers to quickly prepare the fourfold army and set out for a stroll in the gardens during the night."
At that time, having received the king’s command, the ministers immediately arrayed the fourfold army and went quickly to the king’s presence, saying:
"The fourfold army has assembled; this is precisely the right time for Your Majesty to go forth on a pleasure excursion."
At that time, the king placed a great maṇi-jewel atop his banner to lead the way before him, and set out for the pleasure groves during the night.

The radiance of those jewels illuminated one yojana; the fourfold army of the king was entirely bathed in light, with their splendors reflecting one another like the radiance of the heavens, without any difference.
"O Bhikṣus!
This is called the appearance of the sixth great maṇi-jewel when a Wheel-turning King appears.
Furthermore, O Bhikṣus!"

When a Wheel-Turning King appears, there also emerges the Woman-Jewel (strī-ratna), whose physical appearance is of the highest quality, with all her limbs perfectly complete and most excellent; among all people in the world, there is none equal to her. She is light, delicate, and soft like *karkarī* cotton, and from all the pores of her body issues a sublime fragrance.
It is like a precious vessel filled with incense, whose fragrance is ever-present at all times.
Furthermore, every inhalation and exhalation of the Woman Jewel is like the scent of the blue lotus, which is cherished and delighted in by all people.

Following behind the king as he goes about his affairs, the Woman Jewel acts with grace and ease in all her undertakings; she is chaste and upright by nature, untainted by wickedness, always uttering words of love that people delight to hear, and possessing a radiance on her face that people rejoice to behold.
"O Bhikṣus!
This is called the appearance of the seventh jewel, the woman-jewel, at the time when a Wheel-Turning King appears.
Thus spoke the Buddha to the Bhikṣus.
"This is what is called the appearance of the seven treasures when a Wheel-Turning King appears.
You should know that when a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha appears, he proclaims the Dharma of the seven factors of enlightenment."
What are the seven?

They are the awakening factor of mindfulness, the awakening factor of investigation of phenomena, the awakening factor of energy, the awakening factor of rapture, the awakening factor of tranquility, the awakening factor of concentration, and the awakening factor of equanimity. These are called the seven factors of awakening.

Except for when a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha appears in the world and proclaims it, just as with the seven treasures mentioned before, so it is here: except when a Great Anointed Wheel-Turning King appears, these jewels do not manifest.

"You should know that the Dharma of the seven factors of enlightenment taught by the Tathāgata causes all sentient beings to practice according to the truth, so that they may all obtain peace, happiness, and benefit; you should diligently train yourselves in this manner."
The Sūtra on the Seven Jewels of the Wheel-Turning King Spoken by the Buddha.
